newsitem.title: USA: South African firm pleads no contest on arms charges.
newsitem.headline: South African firm pleads no contest on arms charges.

text.p: A South African state-owned arms firm and its subsidiary pleaded "no contest" on Thursday to violating a U.S. arms embargo against South Africa's apartheid-era government, federal prosecutors announced.

State-owned Armament Corp. of South Africa (Armscor) and its subsidiary, Kentron Party Ltd., issued the pleas in U.S. District Court for Eastern Pennsylvania, the U.S. Attorney's office for the district said in a release.
Under U.S. law, a plea of no contest is treated as a guilty plea, though the defendant does not admit wrongdoing.
Armscor was fined $1 million and Kentron was fined $500,000.
In addition, privately owned Fuchs Electronics Pty Ltd, also of South Africa, pleaded guilty on 11 related charges and was fined $10 million.

The firms were charged with working with a Lancaster, Pennsylvania, private firm, International Signal and Control Corp. to smuggle munitions, restricted commodities and technology made in the United States to South Africa's apartheid government between 1978 and 1989.
Seven American defendants, including the International Signal chief executive, previously entered guilty pleas related to the indictment, and an eighth was convicted in a jury trial.
In the plea agreement, Armscor and Kentron acknowledged that they obtained shipments from International Signal by routing them through front companies.
